To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TGF- β-induced TG2 promotes ovarian tumor metastasis and stemness by inducing EMT.
TG2 expression in ovarian cancer cells is induced by TGFβ, a cytokines involved in tumor dissemination, and that this is mediated by the transcription factors SMADs and NF-κB.
TGF-ß-induced TG2 expression and activity in OC cells is regulated by SMADs, and that TGF-Β induces TG2-mediated EMT, formation spheroids and metastasis in OC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of TGF-β in ovarian cancer progression.
the identification of new molecular pathways in the development and progression of ovarian cancer.

understanding the molecular mechanisms that control the metastatic potential of ovarian cancer cells and the development of novel therapies that target these mechanisms to prevent ovarian tumor metastasis and improve survival of patients with ovarian cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TGF- β induces TG2 in OC and that TG2 is required for the formation of spheroid structures, a prerequisite for peritoneal metastasis.
TGF- β-induced TG2 enhances metastasis of ovarian cancer cells by promoting EMT and a stem cell-like phenotype.
TGF-Β induced TG2 enhances ovarian cancer metastasis by inducing epithelial-mesenchymall transition and a cancer stem-cell phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TG2 is a key player in TGF-β induced ovarian tumor metastasis.
TGF- β induced TG2 regulates E-MT, spheroid formation and ovarian tumor dissemination by promoting cancer stem cell phenotype.
TG2 links TGF-ß, EMT and cancer stem cell phenotypes, and is a potential therapeutic target for OC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TG2 is an attractive target for the development of novel therapies for OC.

TG2 expression and activity in ovarian cancer cells is induced by the TGF-β cytokine, a major player in the ovarian cancer microenvironment, and that this induction is a key mechanism by which TGF-β promotes ovarian cancer metastasis.
TG2 is a key mediator of TGF-β signaling, which is involved in ovarian cancer progression and dissemination.
